title: Filtered descent of condensed representing pairs and their chosen-adjoint transpose
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$, with $j$ open and $g$ proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For finite coefficient fields $H\subset\Omega$, let $\mathcal C_H^c(T)$ be the bounded constructible condensed-module categories, with scalar extensions $T^T_{H,H'}$; let $\mathcal C_\Omega^c(T)$ use the finite-extension-valued condensed ring $\underline\Omega$, whose sections on a profinite set are continuous maps with image contained in one finite intermediate field. Use exactly the filtered two-colimit, morphism descent and eventual-equality comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Let $P_H^c=Rg_{*,H}j_{!,H}$ and $P_\Omega^c=Rg_{*,\Omega}j_{!,\Omega}$ with their specified scalar comparisons [lem-pur-compact-support-condensed-realization].

Fix $M_E^c\in\mathcal C_E^c(X)$ and $L_E^c\in\mathcal C_E^c(Y)$. For each finite $H\supset E$, put $M_H^c=T^X_{E,H}M_E^c$, $L_H^c=T^Y_{E,H}L_E^c$. Suppose given bijections natural in $C\in\mathcal C_H^c(X)$,
$$\beta_{H,C}:\operatorname{Hom}_H(C,M_H^c)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_H(P_H^c C,L_H^c),$$
compatible with every finite extension, with counits $t_H=\beta_{H,M_H^c}(1)$ equal to the scalar extensions of $t_E$. Put $M_\Omega^c=T^X_{E,\Omega}M_E^c$ and $L_\Omega^c=T^Y_{E,\Omega}L_E^c$. There is a unique natural bijection
$$\beta_{\Omega,C}:\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(C,M_\Omega^c)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(P_\Omega^c C,L_\Omega^c)$$
induced by the filtered colimits of the $\beta_{H,C_H}$. It is independent of a finite-field model $C_H$ and of its morphism representatives, and has counit $t_\Omega$ the extension of $t_E$. It is natural in maps of the two represented objects and compatible families of the finite representing maps.

For any specified adjunction $P_\Omega^c\dashv J$ with counit $\epsilon^J$, the transpose $c:M_\Omega^c\to J(L_\Omega^c)$ of $t_\Omega$ is invertible and satisfies $\epsilon^J\circ P_\Omega^c(c)=t_\Omega$. It is natural for those data maps and depends on the specified counit. This assertion assumes finite-field representing bijections, with no integral objects or exceptional towers in its hypotheses.

source.place: Filtered-colimit Hom display, descent of morphisms and eventual equality; sk-prop-sp-unique-adjoint/sk-prop-sp-unique-adjoint-categorical.proof.md for the final transpose. Agent generalization to supplied representing pairs, returned item proof Steps 11–12.

proof.text: Obtain the canonical scalar comparisons using lem-pur-filtered-condensed-canonical-comparisons. For each supplied compatible pair define B_C by Equiv.ofBijective from the explicit extended-counit map, using lem-pur-filtered-condensed-counit-bijective. The counit is a real scalar-extended morphism, with no object chosen from a mere existence theorem.

The finite-stage value formula is lem-pur-filtered-condensed-counit-finite-formula. Functoriality proves naturality and the identity value. For uniqueness, at H=E the induced formula fixes B on the invertible transitivity map e from T_E,Omega(T_E,E M) to T_E,Omega M. Naturality and cancellation of P(e) fix B_M(1), and then fix B_C(u) for all C,u. This avoids extra morphism descent for uniqueness.

Naturality transports the induced formula through any model isomorphism, proving the complete model-independence clause. For a pair map at its common field H, apply the two induced formulas to a and to the identity. Finite pair-map compatibility and the tensor transitivity inverse identities yield the square at e. Cancel P(e) and use naturality to obtain it at every C,u.

For a specified adjunction P adjoint J, postcomposition with the transpose of the extended counit is the composite B_C followed by adj.homEquiv. Both are bijections, so Mathlib isIso_of_yoneda_map_bijective makes the transpose invertible. adj.homEquiv.symm_apply_apply gives the counit equation and injectivity gives uniqueness. Replace the second bijection in a pair-map square by its unique explicit counit formula; apply left and right naturality of adj.homEquiv to the counit square. This proves transpose naturality. The IsDescent conjunction and uniqueness give the original exists-unique statement.
